questions.prompt: What is the dimension of the matrix $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The matrix has 2 rows and 3 columns, so it's $2 \times 3$.

questions.prompt: In the augmented matrix, the coefficients and constant terms are separated by a ___ line.
In the matrix $\begin{bmatrix} 4 & -2 \\ 0 & 5 \end{bmatrix}$, what is the entry $a_{22}$? (Enter a number)
Which of the following is NOT an elementary row operation?
options: B. Multiply a row by a nonzero constant
C. Add a multiple of one row to another
D. Multiply a row by zero
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Multiplying a row by zero is not allowed.

questions.prompt: The entry in the second row, first column of a matrix $A$ is denoted by $a_{___}$.
If a variable is missing in an equation, what number should appear in its column of the augmented matrix? (Enter a number)
The notation $R_2 \leftrightarrow R_3$ means:
questions.feedbackIfWrong: It means swap row 2 and row 3.

questions.prompt: After performing $-2R_1 + R_3 \to R_3$, the row that is changed is row ___.
In a row-echelon matrix, the first nonzero entry in each row is called a leading 1. What number is it? (Enter a number)
A matrix in row-echelon form can be solved by:
In reduced row-echelon form, every column with a leading 1 has zeros in all ___ positions.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: All other positions in that column must be zero.

questions.prompt: From the RREF matrix $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & | & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & | & -2 \end{bmatrix}$, what is the value of $y$? (Enter a number)
If an augmented matrix has a row $[0\ 0\ 0\ |\ 4]$, the system is:
options: B. Consistent with infinitely many solutions

questions.prompt: The process of reducing a matrix to reduced row-echelon form is called ___-Jordan elimination.
In the matrix $\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$, to get a leading 1 in the first row, which rows should you swap? (Enter the row numbers, e.g., 1 and 2)
When are two matrices equal?
options: A. When they have the same number of entries
B. When they have the same dimensions and all corresponding entries are equal
C. When they can be added
D. When their determinants are equal
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Two matrices are equal if they have the same dimensions and all corresponding entries are equal.

questions.prompt: To add two matrices, you add their ___ entries.
What does scalar multiplication of a matrix by $c$ do? (Answer the operation: multiply each entry by c)
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Scalar multiplication multiplies every entry of the matrix by that scalar.

questions.prompt: Which operation is generally NOT commutative?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Matrix multiplication is generally not commutative.

questions.prompt: For $AB$ to be defined, the number of ___ of $A$ must equal the number of rows of $B$.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The number of columns of A must equal the number of rows of B.

questions.prompt: Compute $\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}$. (Enter a number)
What is the result of $A + (-A)$?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Adding a matrix and its negative yields the zero matrix.

questions.prompt: To solve $2X = A$ for $X$, multiply $A$ by the scalar ___.
In the matrix addition $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$, what is the entry in row 1, column 2? (Enter a number)
Which property is illustrated by $c(A + B) = cA + cB$?
The product of a $2\times 3$ matrix and a $3\times 1$ matrix is a matrix of dimension ___$\times 1$.
If $3X = \begin{bmatrix} 9 & -6 \\ 0 & 12 \end{bmatrix}$, what is the entry in row 2, column 2 of $X$? (Enter a number)
What is the zero matrix?
options: A. A matrix with all entries equal to 1
B. A matrix with all entries equal to 0
D. A matrix with no entries
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The zero matrix has all entries zero.

questions.prompt: When writing the augmented matrix, if an equation is missing the $y$ variable, the coefficient in the $y$ column is ___.
A $3 \times 3$ matrix has a main diagonal consisting of entries $a_{11}, a_{22},$ and ___.
